title: Stand and Model (2025)
headline: Proposition 1 is false as stated and Algorithm 1 can cycle. The authors disagree; their position is summarised below.

claims.label: Proposition 1
claims.gist: Platform profit is concave in the buyer fee.
claims.statement: For every fixed seller fee, the platform's equilibrium profit is a concave function of the buyer fee.

result.summary: A parameter choice where profit has two local maxima in the buyer fee.
result.witness: With cross-side benefits 0.6 and 0.3 and seller fee 2, profit as a function of the buyer fee has two local maxima, so it is not concave.
result.tested: A grid of cross-side benefits and fees; profit computed in closed form at every grid point.
not_claimed: It is not claimed that an optimal buyer fee fails to exist.
Results that use only the existence of an optimum are not affected.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session, not given the earlier result, recomputed the profit curve.
The researcher derived the profit function by hand.
After the authors' reply, an outside researcher (fictional) checked the example against the printed model.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Algorithm 1
claims.gist: Simultaneous fee updating converges to the optimal fees.
claims.statement: Starting from any fees, simultaneous best-response updating of the two fees (Algorithm 1) converges to the profit-maximising fees.
conditions: both fees updated in the same round
claims.quantifiers: from every initial pair of fees

result.summary: Oscillates between two fee pairs from a symmetric start.
result.witness: From equal initial fees, the two updates overshoot in opposite directions and alternate between two fee pairs indefinitely.
result.tested: Initial fees on a grid for the parameter range of Proposition 1.
not_claimed: Sequential updating of one fee at a time is not claimed to fail.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session reproduced the oscillation.
The researcher traced the updates by hand.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

author_position.summary: The authors consider the intended model to bound cross-side benefits more tightly, which would exclude both examples. The record reports the model as printed; the tighter bound does not appear in the paper.

history.label: Both findings reproduced by the researcher
Additional outside check after the dispute: confirms

statements.ai_use: Discovery and the separate rechecks used AI models in separate sessions. The independent reproduction, the version-of-record check and every editorial decision were done by the researcher.
